title: Help With the Track
can_do: 遇到具体困难时，请求恰好够用的帮助，同时保留自己完成任务的机会。
trigger: A loose track piece will not connect, so the train cannot continue. Child asks Dad for help and must specify which side Dad should hold.
core_response: This won't fit. Can you help me?
stretch_response: Can you help me hold the box?
repair_response: This side. Hold it here, please.
setting: Connecting a short toy train track at a low table.
essential_props: a short toy train track with one loose connecting piece and one train

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: This won't fit. Can you help me?

turns.speaker: child
turns.line: This side. Hold it here, please.

turns.speaker: dad
turns.line: That fits. Try your train now.

replay_cards.title: Open the lunch box
replay_cards.change: The box slides when Child tries to lift its latch
replay_cards.challenge: Child says, 'Can you help me hold the box?' Dad asks where to hold it. Child points to the side away from the latch. Dad steadies that side, Child lifts the latch and opens the lid, then confirms it is open.

replay_cards.title: Zip the coat
replay_cards.change: The zipper has been started but its bottom lifts when Child pulls
replay_cards.challenge: Child asks Mom for help and points to the bottom of the zipper. Mom holds the joined base steady while Child pulls the zipper up. Child checks that the coat is closed, and they go outside together.

parent_support: Let him show the join that will not connect; ask which side needs support if his first request is unclear.
Hold only the side he identifies and let him connect the piece. The useful sequence is adult support first, then his own action.
Keep the train near Dad until he requests it, then let him test the repaired track. A brief puzzled look is enough; help is ordinary and does not require visible distress.
